title: RSA Launches Agentic Identity Platform to Secure AI Agents and MCP Servers
content_md: RSA has unveiled RSA Agent ID, an agentic identity security platform designed to help highly regulated organizations discover, secure, and govern artificial intelligence agents and Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers . Announced at The AI Conference in San Francisco, the platform targets financial institutions, government agencies, and critical-infrastructure operators facing growing accountability, sovereignty, and compliance demands around autonomous AI activity. The launch reflects a broader shift in enterprise security: AI agents are increasingly treated as operational identities rather than isolated software tools. RSA Launches Agentic Identity Platform These systems hold credentials, access sensitive applications, execute workflows, and may take actions involving payments, customer data, classified information, or production infrastructure. RSA said many organizations still lack a complete inventory of the agents running across their environments, who is accountable for them, and the controls needed to stop risky activity. RSA Agent ID is built around three modules: Discover, Secure, and Govern. The Discover component identifies sanctioned and shadow AI agents and MCP servers across identity, cloud, endpoint, and gateway telemetry. It registers them as first-class identities, assigning a named owner, risk classification, lifecycle state, and relationship to the organization’s existing identity provider.
